1.explanation: The CodeSnippet component is responsible for rendering the CopyButton in single mode and originally applied an inline style { position: 'absolute', top: '1rem', right: '1rem' } when type==='single'. In the current compressed code that style prop is missing, so the CopyButton falls back to its base CSS (.bx--copy-btn), which sets position: relative. As a result the copy button is no longer anchored to the snippet’s top right. Fixing this requires restoring or properly applying the inline style in CodeSnippet (or adjusting CopyButton’s default CSS) so that position: absolute is enforced in single mode.
1.bug_scenario: When a CodeSnippet is rendered in “single” mode, its copy-to-clipboard button is appearing in the wrong place (nested inside the snippet rather than pinned to its top right). The screenshot shows the button shifted down because the default .bx--copy-btn class applies position: relative, and the inline style that ought to force position: absolute is missing or being overridden.

2.explanation: The CodeSnippet component used to pass an inline style prop to the CopyButton in single mode to force { position: 'absolute', top: '1rem', right: '1rem' }. In the current compressed source, that style prop is missing, so the CopyButton reverts to its default .bx--copy-btn CSS (position: relative). Restoring the conditional style assignment on CopyButton inside the CodeSnippet render function is the key fix point.
2.bug_scenario: In single‐mode CodeSnippet, the copy icon now appears shoved underneath the code rather than floating in the top-right corner as an absolute element. The screenshot shows the copy button rendered in the normal flow (relative positioning) inside the snippet container, instead of positioned absolutely.
